raw_recipe.headline: Marinated Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: For this easy-to-follow recipe, pork tenderloin marinates in sherry, cinnamon, brown sugar and soy sauce, for sweet, moist and tender results.

recipeInstructions.text: Place soy sauce, brown sugar, sherry, dried onion, cinnamon, olive oil, and a touch of garlic powder in a large resealable plastic bag. Seal, and shake to mix. Place pork in bag with marinade, seal, and refrigerate for 6 to 12 hours.
Lightly oil grate. Place tenderloins on grill, and discard marinade. Cook 20 minutes, or to desired doneness. Slice into medallions, and serve.

review.reviewBody: Found this fantastic recipe a year ago, have made it several times since for both company and just the family. It is absolutely delicious and it consistently gets rave reviews. Here's what I do: double the marinade, except for the cinnamon. Mince 2 Tbsp. fresh onion in place of dried. I try to marinade all day, but I have found that even a few hours is sufficient. I bake the tenderloins in a 400 oven for about 40 min. And the biggest tip: take the leftover marinade, boil, and add cornstarch or a flour roux to thicken and make a delicious sauce/gravy. Other Tips - #1) don't leave out the sherry. It really makes the recipe. You can buy cream sherry at your local spirits store for around $7 a bottle and you can utlitize it in many recipes. #2) if you are looking for a good side dish to match this pork, try Baked Pineapple Casserole off of this site. It is excellent!!

Didn't change a thing and it was awesome! Marinated it for 12 hours. I don't have an outdoor grill, so I used my cast iron grill pan on the stove. The best part was the chargrilled outer part -- mmmmmmmm! Next time I'll probably sear it on the stovetop and finish it off in the oven. I'll probably also boil and reduce down some of the left over marinade to make a yummy sauce. This is now officially the only pork tenderloin recipe I'll ever need. My husband thought it was amazing, as did my very picky ten year old.




Edited to Add -- Made this a week later (couldn't wait any longer, it was that good) and did just that -- I seared it on the grill pan, stuck in a meat thermometer, and finished it off in a 350 oven until it reached 160, about 25-30 minutes. I boiled the marinade to reduce it to a nice gravy. Mmmmmmm! It was moist throughout and so good. My husband had thirds!

This is the best pork tenderloin recipe!! I have been making this for a couple of years now. The only change that I make is I add minced fresh onion and fresh garlic. I made four tenderloins and mine where about 1.25 lbs each so I tripled the marinade and added about 1 cup of fresh minced onion and about 5 cloves minced garlic. I marinade it for about 24 hours and we always grill it. I like the added cinnamon. I have even froze the tenderloin in the marinade and my son brought it back to college to make and it turns out great! Such amazing flavor! Thank you so much for sharing your recipe!

Loved it. Followed the recipe exactly, doubling the sauce and not doubling the cinnamon. Even my picky 7 year old loved it. I will be making this for my mother-in-law, and that is saying something!! I baked it in a 425 degree oven for about 25 minutes with a meat thermometer set for 160. Mmmm perfect. I served it with potatoes and green beans, but I think I would do rice or quinoa next time.

I've made this recipe several times in the oven (thank you to whoever made the previous comment) at 350 for an hour. I also substituted two Tbsp of balsamic vinegar for the sherry and it was fantastic! Very tender and great flavor!

I thought that the cinnamon might've been a weird flavor, but it just made it taste like it had chinese 5 spice in it (so sort of asian). I only made one change, which is that I replaced the sherry with bourbon because I didn't have sherry, but have lots of bourbon. I also took the marinade and boiled it for a few minutes, just until the blood cooked in it, then strained the blood particles out and returned it to the sauce pan and thickened it to a glaze consistency and served it over the pork. It was delicious. Tasted kind of like Chinese bbq pork, but way easier.

This was fantastic! I didn't have Sherry so I found a substitute online which was 1 Tbsp white vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and 1 Tbsp water and that's what I used. I only had about 2 hours to marinate it and I cooked it in the oven on 350 for 1.5 hours instead of on a grill. It was still amazing! I will be making this again!

I used an indoor grill up to 130 then covered with foil and moved to a 350 oven to push it to internal of 150. Let rest 5-10 min before slicing. I also added thyme to marinade- strain and pour marinade into saucepan and reduce for sauce-delicious!!

I made the marinade as stated, but used a 1 pound tenderloin, and let it marinate over night. Instead of baking it in the oven, I sous vide cooked the tenderloin at 149 degrees for 90 minutes. I saved the marinade to make a sauce as others suggested. The tenderloin came out super tender and moist, but this may have been as a result of the sous vide cooking. It was nicely flavored by the marinade which was not overwhelming. I thought the sauce was OK, but my husband like it a lot. The sauce came out on the thick side, so I probably should have added some water to thin it a bit.

I did follow recipe ingredient list. But I had to alter the cooking process because I didn't have time to marinate the pork. So I simply put the meat and marinade in my pressure cooker. It was delicious. Specifically, I browned the 5/8" thick pork medallions in a bit of olive oil, put them in the pressure cooker with the marinade and set the cooker to 8 minutes. Yum. I then removed the pork, added a Tablespoon of cornstarch to the marinade/juices, stirred until thickened and served over the pork along with mashed potatoes and steamed broccoli with lemon and butter. Yum Yum.

Excellent! Great flavor - beautiful on the grill. Per other recommendations - doubled the marinade except cinnamon. Used fresh onion and garlic instead of powder. Boiled the marinade, added a little corn starch and had a lovely sauce. Thanks for a great recipe - we will be making this again.
Great marinate
We loved this! I subbed brown sugar and reduced pepper a bit but otherwise made as written, in oven at 400 degrees. Thickened marinade was delicious.
Great Pork tenderloin, the best ever
I’ve used this marinade for years. It’s delicious!

The cinnamon makes this recipe! Tonight I varied the recipe a bit and used fresh minced shallots, garlic and subbed brandy for the sherry and only had a chance to marinate 3 hours. Always a delicious marinade!
Left out the garlic and used red wine in place of sherry
Great recipe! I didn’t have Sherry, so I used port wine. I also doubled the marinade minus the cinnamon and later made it into a sauce using some corn starch and water in equal parts(about 1TBSP).

This was a fantastic recipe although I did use fresh minced onion and garlic and did not have sherry so substituted peach balsamic vinegar instead. The next time I make it I will buy some sherry and try it that way. Be sure and double the batch and make a gravy with the marinade.

I have been making this since 2006. I found the recipe right here. Today I decided to review. I use it for pork and boneless chicken. I usually marinate for 24 hours. The only change I make is I don’t add sherry anymore or the dried onions since I don’t use it for anything else. I mix everything in a gallon ziplock, add the meat and throw in fridge. I even freeze the meat uncooked right in the ziplock with the marinade. It’s great to take on vacay frozen uncooked. Makes a good ice pack for cooler if you freeze flat. Enjoy!
